clue.text: Sibyl follows the Conservative leader, showing craft

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, so the first letter of Conservative is taken

parts.note: a sibyl was a prophetess of the ancient world, an oracle

explanation.surface: A prophetess falls in behind the Tory leader and proves to be cunning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like cunning in the surface, but it is a boat: a coracle is a small round wicker boat. 'follows' puts ORACLE after C.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round wicker boat is a type of vessel, and craft is a general word for boats.

clue.text: Self-satisfied top man, one with decent new housing

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer, the man at the top

indicators.note: housing means the rearranged letters of decent enclose the numeral for one
new indicates the letters of decent are made anew in another order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A complacent boss gives a respectable fresh home to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' makes NCETED, the anagram of DECENT, and 'housing' puts I inside it; 'with' is a link. A commanding officer is the top man of a unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Conceited people are vain and pleased with themselves, smug.

clue.text: Many a Greek character turns in others — most odd!

indicators.note: in places the turned letters inside the word for others

parts.note: the rest means the others

indicators.note: turns means the letters for many and the Greek letter read backwards

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many
mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek turns up among the rest, which is very strange!
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' makes UMM of M and MU, which goes 'in' REST.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is British slang for strange or peculiar, so the superlative means strangest.

clue.text: State provision

explanation.definitionFit: A condition is a state, as in good condition, and also a stipulation or proviso in an agreement.

clue.text: A painter — some garret type

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An artist is just the kind who lives in an attic.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on the starving artist in a garret. William Etty was an English painter of nudes.
explanation.definitionFit: William Etty was a nineteenth-century English artist known for nude figure studies.

clue.text: Caught the second involved in a racket

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
the latter is the second of two things mentioned

explanation.surface: Someone who came second got caught up in a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' looks like a criminal scheme, but here it means din.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a loud noise, and a clatter is a rattling din.

clue.text: These little beasts, having chosen meal, changed order

indicators.note: changed order means the letters of chosen meal are put in a different sequence

explanation.surface: Animals that picked their dinner then rearranged it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' is a link; the surface hints at the animals' changing colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Chameleons are small lizards, the beasts known for changing skin colour.

clue.text: Keep off a green

parts.note: vert is green in heraldry

explanation.surface: Stay off the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: VERT is the heraldic word for green.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert is to ward off or turn away a danger.

clue.text: Outstanding evidence of pre historic undertaking

definitions.text: Outstanding evidence of pre historic undertaking

parts.words: Outstanding evidence of pre historic undertaking
parts.note: outstanding means standing out from the land, and undertaking means burying the dead, the work of an undertaker, in ancient times

explanation.definitionFit: An ancient burial mound rises from the ground over a grave, a barrow.

clue.text: Long-legged and heartless guy rushed to be first

parts.note: ran means rushed

indicators.note: heartless means the middle is removed, keeping the first and last letters of guy

explanation.surface: A tall chap without feelings hurried to the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the middle letter of GUY, and 'to be first' moves the word for rushed to the front, though it comes after in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangy describes a tall, slim person with long limbs.

clue.text: Ancient name for ladies only?

explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome the nomen was the family part of a citizen's name; split in two it says no males admitted, as at a women-only event.

clue.text: Dealers need smart product

indicators.note: a product is something made or worked up, so the letters of need smart are made into something new

explanation.surface: Shopkeepers require a stylish item to sell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'product' looks like goods on sale, but it signals the anagram of NEED SMART.
explanation.definitionFit: Tradesmen are shopkeepers and merchants, people who deal in goods.

clue.text: Protection for the pupil

parts.note: reads as something shielding a schoolchild, but the pupil is the dark centre of the eye, which a fold of skin covers

explanation.definitionFit: The fold of skin closing over the eye shields its pupil from dust and light.

clue.text: The thoughtful way in which people register

parts.note: men stands for people in general
to tally is to record or count up, to register

explanation.surface: A considerate manner in which a crowd signs in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which' is a link joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in the mind, by thought, is the adverb's sense: in a thinking manner.

clue.text: Military personnel lie in because it's spring

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

indicators.note: in places the word lie inside the word for because

parts.note: since means because
taken as written

explanation.surface: Soldiers stay in bed late since it is springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lie in' looks like a lazy morning, but 'in' is the container signal. 'it's' is a link; spring is springiness, not the season.
explanation.definitionFit: Resilience is elasticity, the ability to bounce back, which is what spring means here.

clue.text: Band together

parts.note: reads as people uniting, but means the whole orchestra playing at once, a musical direction

explanation.definitionFit: The Italian musical term marks a passage played by all performers at once.

clue.text: Uses drill

explanation.definitionFit: To exercise a right or power is to use it, and exercises are drills, practice routines repeated for training.

clue.text: The rogue known for his 19

explanation.definitionFit: A chiseller is a swindler or cheat, and also a carver who chisels stone, the craft of the clue numbered 19.

clue.text: A property of some taste in the main

definitions.text: A property of some taste in the main

parts.words: A property of some taste in the main
parts.note: reads as a house of fine taste on the whole, but the main is the sea and the property is a quality of flavour

explanation.definitionFit: Seawater has a briny flavour, and this quality of tasting of sodium chloride is the property meant.

clue.text: "A dark illimitable ocean without bound, without — " (Milton)

definitions.text: "A dark illimitable ocean without bound, without — " (Milton)

parts.words: "A dark illimitable ocean without bound, without — " (Milton)
parts.note: a quotation from Paradise Lost, Book II, describing Chaos; the missing word completes the line about boundless space

explanation.definitionFit: Milton's line describes a void lacking measurable extent, completing the phrase about a sea with no size or bound.

clue.text: "Woman Embracing Child", the work of 16

indicators.note: embracing means the woman's name holds the child inside it

parts.note: Mary is a woman's name
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A title for a sculpture of a mother and child, carved by a craftsman.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted title points to Mary and her son. 16 is CHISELLER, here a stone carver.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonework made by a mason or carver is the product of the chiseller's trade.

clue.text: The first person to make a distribution exemplary

parts.note: I is the first person singular pronoun
a deal is the distribution of cards to the players

explanation.surface: Someone takes the lead in sharing things out and sets a fine example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something exemplary serves as a perfect model, which is what an ideal is.

clue.text: Date certain to be a wash-out

parts.note: an era is a period, a date in history
sure means certain

explanation.surface: An appointment that is bound to be a flop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is a link; wash-out means something washed away, not a failure.
explanation.definitionFit: An erasure is a rubbing out or removal, something wiped away.

clue.text: Blissful area of London still

parts.note: EC is the East Central postal district of London, the City
still means not moving, static

explanation.surface: A part of London that never changes is delightful.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the postcode for the City, London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstatic means overwhelmed with joy, a state of perfect happiness.

clue.text: When no longer cold the Spanish are superior

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
C is short for cold, as on a tap
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Once it stops being chilly the people of Spain come out on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to outdo others, to be better than them.

clue.text: Puff over a work-out, though fit

indicators.note: over means the advert sits on top of the rest in this down entry

parts.note: a puff is a promotional notice, an ad
PT is physical training, a work-out

explanation.surface: Gasping after a gym session, though in good shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puff' looks like panting, but it is an advertisement. 'though' is a link; 'fit' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt something is to adjust it, to make it suitable.

clue.text: An Asian with English mate in Northern Ireland

indicators.note: in places the Englishman and his friend inside the abbreviation for the province

parts.note: pal is a friend, a mate

explanation.surface: Someone from Asia is in Belfast with an English friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins English and mate, which then go together inside NI.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nepali is a person from Nepal, a Himalayan country of South Asia.

clue.text: A bluff about stuff which is worn

parts.note: C is short for circa, about
a rag is a scrap of worn cloth

explanation.surface: A deception concerning clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bluff' looks like a deception, but it is a steep cliff.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluff is a steep cliff or headland, a rocky outcrop.

clue.text: Move east in carton or crate

indicators.note: move tells us to shift the letters of east, in and carton into a new order

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions for shifting goods eastwards packed in a box or case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Move' signals the anagram of E, IN and CARTON; 'or' links it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A crate is a box for transporting goods, a kind of receptacle.

clue.text: See employment is provided for the parasite

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
use is the employment of something

explanation.surface: Look, work is laid on for the hanger-on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is provided for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A louse is a small wingless insect living on its host, a classic bloodsucking pest.

clue.text: Delayed accepting further baby-clothes

indicators.note: accepting means the word for delayed takes the word for further inside it

parts.note: delayed means late
yet means further or still more, as in yet another

explanation.surface: Someone running behind takes in more outfits for an infant.
explanation.definitionFit: A layette is a complete set of garments and bedding for a newborn.

clue.text: Fish catches — in stones

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish
nets means catches, as a fisherman does

explanation.surface: A fisherman hauls in a fish among the rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link; 'stones' are gems, not rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Garnets are red semi-precious gems, so precious stones.
